# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-6

## Summary

The shrimp feeding pathway implementation is well-engineered with tight mass conservation. All 8 feeding pathway tests and 22 budget tracking tests pass. The core routing in `route_consumed_food` correctly partitions consumed N and C through feces (→ fine detritus), excretion (→ TAN + DOC), respiration (→ DIC + O2 demand), and retention (→ reserve_g). Budget accounting is consistent: body composition constants (27.59 mg N/g, 172.41 mg C/g) were chosen to exactly match the `feed_n_to_c_ratio = 0.16` organic matter decomposition, ensuring perfect budget neutrality across death routing, hatching, and maturation. The invariants system validates routing fraction sums on save/load. No critical bugs found. Three amendments proposed: (1) document the biologically questionable coupling of N excretion to O2 availability in the respiration-limited path, (2) add an output-side mass closure assertion in route_consumed_food, and (3) explicitly document the missing maintenance drain on reserve_g as a known gap for dependent beads.

## Amendments

1. In `route_consumed_food` (shrimp.rs:266), when O2 limits respiration, the unrespired N is routed to `reserve_g` instead of being released as TAN. Add a code comment explaining the biological rationale for this choice (or lack thereof). In real shrimp physiology, nitrogen excretion continues even under hypoxia because deamination is not directly O2-dependent. If the intent is to keep the implementation simple and mass-conserving, document that this is an intentional simplification that overestimates reserve accumulation and underestimates TAN release under low-DO conditions. This matters because downstream N-budget diagnostics would show misleadingly low TAN production whenever DO is depleted.
   Rationale: The current code couples N excretion to O2 availability via `respiration_scale`, but biological N excretion from amino acid catabolism is largely O2-independent. Under hypoxia, real shrimp still excrete ammonia. The simplification is mass-safe but produces a biologically inverted signal: low DO → less TAN → looks like lower bioload, when reality is the opposite. A comment would prevent future maintainers from mistaking this for an intentional physiological model.
2. Add a `debug_assert!` or inline comment in `route_consumed_food` (shrimp.rs:197-271) confirming that the total mass routed (fecal + excreted_N + excreted_C + respired_C + respired_N + retained) equals consumed_n_mg + consumed_c_mg. The existing `debug_assert!` at lines 172-178 only checks the input side (consumed_route_g vs elemental_food_mass_g). A matching assertion on the output side of `route_consumed_food` would close the loop and catch any future refactoring that breaks the partition, especially given the O2-limited spillover path which adjusts multiple destinations simultaneously.
   Rationale: The routing function has a complex O2-limited spillover path that adjusts respired C, respired N, and retained mass in tandem. A single-line `debug_assert!` at the end of the function confirming output-side mass closure would catch regressions from future changes to the spillover logic, complementing the input-side assertion that already exists.
3. The `reserve_g` pool grows monotonically (shrimp.rs:262-270) with no maintenance metabolism drain. For multi-year simulations, this means the organic reserve approaches the entire mass of consumed food minus respiration/excretion/feces, making condition_index disconnected from actual energetic state. Add a TODO or tracking issue reference indicating that a maintenance drain (reserve → respiration at basal metabolic rate) is needed before this pathway can be considered complete, and document the expected magnitude (e.g., a fraction of reserve consumed per day as basal metabolism).
   Rationale: The bead spec says 'Track assimilated reserve/condition explicitly enough that later shrimp realism work can build on the same pathway.' The reserve field exists but without any drain, condition_index is driven entirely by environmental factors (DO, NH3, food availability) and never by the reserve level itself. This means reserve accumulates without bound, which will produce unrealistic behavior when the dependent beads (tanksim-6e5.6.1, tanksim-6e5.6.2) build on this pool. Documenting the gap explicitly would prevent the dependent beads from assuming reserve already represents energetic state.
